The open gap is whether either button path reaches it with the same inputs, so I’m scanning the image and disassembling those paths.The image shows a shared writer and a separate custom-button route. Equality of the two records is still open, so I’m writing that as conclusion (c) with the new listings.**Conclusion (c).** Stock AF-ON and stock half-press are not shown to publish the same ten-byte target record. The shared writer is real; equal inputs, equal shadow state, and a rebuild on each button edge are not.

`work/result.md` and `work/evidence-manifest.json` are in place. Confirmed r1 listings were left as they were. The correction is under `work/out/r2/`.

What the image does show:

- `0x609b3c79` still has the same seven inputs, the kind-2 position force, the priority clear, and the shadow replace. The second `0xe951` store is at `0x609b39f0`.
- Direct rebuilds go through the pose-group change at `0x60447de4`, or through the accessor when the record is dirty. Neither S1 `0x610aef37` nor the custom-button down body calls that chain directly.
- Default-route AF-ON down is row `0x6131be80` → `0x610a2407` → `0x610a25f1`. Table value 10 calls `0x610a5620` with mode 1 at `0x610a267f`. The handler does not show that every press arrives with value 10.
- Cached `0x90a1[1] == 0` calls `0x609025aa` only when `0xa33ca30d` is also 0. That path calls `0x6004cdf8` and sometimes `0x6004cefd`. The earlier claim that this byte cannot affect any record byte is withdrawn.
- T9d’s K1 record stays with T9d. T7’s session left the record at 0 and did not enter the writer.

The zone table in `work/out/r2/zone-table-r2.md` marks every zone, both poses, and the release path as not decided. No instruction was found that stores a different byte for one button.
